manufacturer_data.description: Govee parses goodsType from manufacturer-specific data bytes in the scan record. Plug family goodsTypes: 50=dual, 90=triple. Exact byte encoding TBD (needs HCI snoop).

device.name: Govee H5080 Smart Plug
device.notes:
BLE smart plug family from Govee. The H5080 protocol is DISTINCT from the H6001 bulb family — it uses custom 128-bit UUIDs (not the standard 16-bit SIG-assigned space) and has its own command structure.
Family members: - H5080: single plug - H5081: single plug variant - H5083: dual plug (goodsType=50) - H5085: single plug with Matter support - H5089: triple plug (goodsType=90) - H5160: triple plug variant
CONFIDENCE: LOW-MEDIUM. UUIDs confirmed from APK static analysis. Command byte format inferred from CmdTurn.java — bits 0-3 carry on/off state, bits 4-7 carry port selector. Needs HCI snoop to verify exact packet structure.

credentials.notes: BLE-only; no WiFi passphrase crosses the link. No authentication was found, so anyone in range can switch the outlet — worth surfacing, given this controls mains power.

factory_reset.effect: Not established. The plug is BLE-only and holds no network credential or binding, so there may be nothing a reset would clear; no reset command was recovered from the app. Cutting mains power is the only state change confirmed, and it is not known to clear anything.

methods.description: Expected: no provisioning needed. Scan, connect, write commands.

steps.action: Power the plug and scan for BLE advertisements.

setup.notes: Likely no pairing required, consistent with Govee's BLE product philosophy. Device advertises on power-up.

rejoin.notes: The plug joins no network and holds no bond. Any client may connect once the previous one disconnects.

turn_on.description: Turn outlet on (port 0). Port is encoded in the command byte.

characteristics.name: Control Write / Notify
characteristics.notes:
Primary control characteristic. Commands use IoT-style JSON with cmd type "turn". The CmdTurn class encodes on/off state in a single byte: - Bits 0-3: on/off state (1=port0 on, 2=port1 on, 4=port2 on, 15=all on) - Bits 4-7: port selector (16=port0, 32=port1, 64=port2)
Example: byte 0x11 = port 0 on (0x10 | 0x01)
         byte 0x21 = port 1 on (0x20 | 0x02)
         byte 0x10 = port 0 off (0x10 | 0x00)

TBD: Need HCI snoop to confirm exact wire format and framing. The byte values below are derived from the app's CmdTurn bit encoding above (port 0), not captured on the wire — hence hypothesis. Earlier revisions listed both on and off as 0x00, which cannot be right: off still carries the port selector, so port-0 off is 0x10, and on is 0x11.
